data.name: Raj
data.gender_notes: Raj is used as a male name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit root rāj, 'to rule, shine' — rāja, 'king'. Its root is Sanskrit rāj (राज्). A classical Sanskrit term for a king. Raj is a Sanskrit name meaning “King; kingdom; rule”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Raj expresses “King; kingdom; rule”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit root rāj, 'to rule, shine' — rāja, 'king'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Raj total 11, reducing to 2. Number 2 is associated with cooperation, sensitivity and balance.

vedic_reference.note: The name 'Raj' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'rāja' which means 'ruler', 'king', or 'sovereign'. It is a common name in Hindu mythology and appears in various Puranas and Itihasas. In the Vedas, 'Rajas' is one of the three gunas, representing passion, desire, and material attachment.
